thread:
alice.net: FYI — customer AcmeCorp (Private / VPC) started seeing 503/504s to private endpoints after AWS DX maintenance overnight. They say traffic fell back to IPsec but sessions are flapping.

inc-bot: Incident created for channel incidents by alice.net — priority P1.

sam.support: Which region and connection type? DX primary or just VPN? Any logs from customer?

alice.net: us-east-1. Primary was Direct Connect (l2), with an IPsec VPN as failover. Customer says DX went down briefly then IPsec didn't remain stable. They see TLS handshake failures from app -> private endpoint.

rachel.sre: Can you grab the gateway IPsec/BGP state and a tcpdump from the edge? Basics: `show ip bgp summary`, `show ipsec sa` and `tcpdump -n -i eth0 'udp port 500 or udp port 4500 or proto 50'`

alice.net: Pasting sanitized outputs from our gateway: 

```
# show ipsec sa
Tunnel to 198.51.100.10: IKE: ESTABLISHED, CHILD_SA: INSTALLED
  last_updown: 2026-02-22T02:13:54Z
  remote-id: 198.51.100.10
  ike_sa_state: up
  ipsec_sa_state: down (no SA)
  last_message: AUTH_FAILED (no matching proposal)
```

```
# show bgp neighbors 10.0.1.1
BGP neighbor 10.0.1.1 in state Active, last reset 00:02:13, last error: connection closed
```

alice.net: Customer tcpdump shows a lot of "ICMP frag needed" from intermediate router and UDP 4500 packets but ESP traffic seems missing. Suspect MTU / fragmentation or a NAT-T issue.

jordan.eng: Could be PMTU blackhole or an ACL on their side blocking ESP (proto 50) so only NAT-T UDP 4500 goes through but fragmented packets get dropped. Also check if our NAT IP changed after DX failover and customer egress allowlist didn't include it.

sam.support: Asking Acme to run quick checks: `traceroute -T` / `traceroute -I` to our gateway, and verify their firewall allows UDP 500/4500 and proto 50 to our gateway IPs and also allows ICMP Type 3 Code 4 (fragmentation needed). Also ask for BGP neighbor state from their side.

alice.net: Customer returned these snippets: 

```
# tcpdump -n host 198.51.100.10
12:03:01.123456 IP 203.0.113.8.4500 > 198.51.100.10.4500: UDP, length 312
12:03:01.125000 ICMP 10.0.0.1 unreachable > 203.0.113.8: fragmentation needed, mtu 1400
```

# Their BGP shows neighbor stuck in Active and our last-update shows repeated keepalive timeouts.

rachel.sre: That confirms fragmentation/MTU — large ESP packets are being dropped. Immediate mitigations: 1) enable MSS clamping / TCP MSS to 1360 on both sides, 2) enable NAT-T keepalives and lower DPD timers so tunnels recover faster, 3) ensure egress allowlist includes our NAT IPs used for VPN after DX failover.

net-oncall: I'm going to apply a temporary MSS clamp (1360) and ensure iptables allows UDP 500/4500 + proto 50. Pushing now.

jordan.eng: Also adjust the kernel xfrm settings to accept fragmented ESP - `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc=0` and verify `iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu` if not already present.

net-oncall: Applied MSS clamp and opened UDP 500/4500 + ESP on the gateway. Restarted ipsec service.

```
# show ipsec sa (after change)
Tunnel to 198.51.100.10: IKE: ESTABLISHED, CHILD_SA: INSTALLED
  ipsec_sa_state: up
```

```
# show bgp neighbors 10.0.1.1
BGP neighbor 10.0.1.1 in state Established,  routes accepted: 520
```

alice.net: Customer confirms prefixes now present and API errors subsided. They saw reconnection around 12:07 UTC.

sam.support: Great — can you collect artifacts for postmortem: full tcpdump (pcap), `ip xfrm state`, `ip xfrm policy`, `iptables -t mangle -L -n -v`, and kernel sysctls before/after change? Also note timestamp of our NAT IP during DX failover.

rachel.sre: Root cause hypothesis: DX failover triggered our egress NAT to change IPs; customer egress allowlist didn't include the backup NAT IP and their firewall/edge dropped large ESP fragments when NAT-T was in use, causing BGP/SA failures. Contributing: strict ICMP deny (no fragmentation-needed) and no MSS clamping on the path.

jordan.eng: Action items: (1) Document recommended network checklist for Private customers with DX/ExpressRoute + IPsec fallback (allow proto 50, UDP 500/4500, ICMP frag-needed, include backup NAT IPs), (2) Add automated check in onboarding to verify egress allowlist coverage, (3) Add MSS clamp default for gateways serving DX fallback, (4) Update runbook for support to include tcpdump snippets and exact commands.

alice.net: I'll own the support follow-ups with Acme and create a postmortem doc. Thanks net-oncall + eng on rapid fix.

inc-bot: Incident resolved (status: mitigated) — followup: create postmortem and assign owners.

sam.support: Closing thread, please ping if any regression.
